question: If the average of ten numbers is 50 and the average of the first six numbers is 45, what is the average of the last four numbers?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The overall average of 10 numbers is 50.

The first 6 numbers have an average of 45, causing a net deviation of 6 × (45 − 50) = −30.

To balance the overall average to 50, the last 4 numbers must have a compensating deviation of +30.

The average deviation for the last 4 numbers = +30 ÷ 4 = +7.5.

Average of the last 4 numbers = 50 + 7.5 = 57.5.

**∴ The correct answer is 57.5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total numbers = 10

Average of 10 numbers = 50

Number of first items = 6

Average of first 6 numbers = 45

**Formula Used:**

Sum of items = Average × Total number of items

 
 
 First 6 Numbers
 Avg = 45 | Sum = 270
 
 
 
 Last 4 Numbers
 Avg = ? | Sum = 230

 
 
 Total 10 Numbers (Overall Average = 50)
 Total Sum = 10 × 50 = 500
 
 
 
• 
 
• 
 
• 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total sum of all 10 numbers = 10 × 50 = 500

⇒ Sum of the first 6 numbers = 6 × 45 = 270

⇒ Sum of the last 4 numbers = Total sum − Sum of first 6 numbers

⇒ Sum of the last 4 numbers = 500 − 270 = 230

⇒ Average of the last 4 numbers = 230 ÷ 4

⇒ Average of the last 4 numbers = 57.5

**∴ The correct answer is 57.5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average

When combining two different groups of sizes n₁ and n₂ with averages A₁ and A₂, the combined average is calculated as (n₁ × A₁ + n₂ × A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Deviation Method

The net sum of deviations of all observations from their arithmetic mean is always exactly zero. Balancing the positive and negative deviations provides the fastest way to compute missing averages without heavy multiplication.

Replacement Method

When a new observation replaces an old one in a set, the value of the new observation can be directly calculated as: New Value = Old Value + (Increase/Decrease in Average × Total Number of Items).
